transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... I guess I'm just having some trouble with... making stupid mistakes on things. I've been doing applications lately, and some research notes, and... I just keep turning them in with these small errors. 

Like, I'll put the wrong date on an artwork, or just skip a question entirely. It's kind of embarrassing, honestly. Especially since I... I really thought I had checked them over before handing them in. So... yeah. That's why I'm here.

When you're not working on applications or research notes, do you find it hard to focus and pay attention to other things in your everyday life, or does this problem mainly happen with these specific tasks?

Um... I guess it happens with other things, too. Like... if I'm just trying to read or write at my desk. It doesn't really take much to lose my place. A siren outside, or... people talking in the hallway. Sometimes even just a random thought about an exhibit idea or something. I'll just... get pulled away by it. And then twenty minutes go by before I even notice. So... yeah. It's not just the applications.
How long have you been experiencing these attention problems? Have you had trouble focusing like this since you were younger, or is this something that's been happening more recently?

Um... I guess it's been a while. Since I was younger, yeah. 

Like... even back in elementary school, my teachers would put on my report cards that I had good ideas, but... I'd just forget to turn in worksheets. Or I'd lose the instructions for things. Miss the little details. It was... it was always like that unless my parents went through my backpack every night to check everything. So... yeah, it's not new.
Do you find yourself fidgeting a lot, having trouble sitting still, or feeling like you have excess energy that's hard to control?
Um... no, not really. I don't... I don't really have that issue. I just sit there. I'm not... I'm not bouncing off the walls or anything.
When you're in conversations with friends or family, do you find yourself interrupting people, or blurting things out before thinking them through?
Um... no. I don't think so. I usually just... wait for them to finish talking. I don't really blurt things out.

How much has this difficulty with attention and making careless mistakes affected your ability to do well in school or work, or to maintain relationships? Has it caused you real problems in your life?

Um... I guess it causes some issues. Nothing crazy, but... yeah. 

I've, uh, submitted some work late. And I missed a couple of application deadlines recently. Just... lost track of them, I guess. My mentor actually brought it up not too long ago. He just said my lack of follow-through is starting to hurt opportunities I should be ready for. So... yeah, I guess it does affect things.
When you're sitting down trying to relax or watch something, do you find yourself feeling restless or like you need to be doing something? Or do you feel okay just sitting and being still?
Um... no. I feel fine just sitting. I don't really get restless or anything... I can just sit and watch whatever.
At work or in your classes, do your teachers or supervisors comment on your attention problems, or do you mainly notice them yourself when you're trying to focus?
Um... not really. I think it's mostly just me. Like... I just notice it myself when I'm trying to get things done. They don't really say anything about it.
Do you ever find yourself getting frustrated or angry quickly when things don't go the way you expected, or when you're trying to concentrate and keep getting distracted?
Um... no. Not really. I don't think I get angry quickly. Just... I don't know, normal, I guess. I don't really get frustrated like that.
Looking back to when you were a kid, did your parents or teachers ever say you were hyperactive, or that you had trouble sitting still, or that you were impulsive or acted without thinking?
Um... no, I don't think so. I don't remember anyone saying that. I wasn't really... hyper or anything. Just kind of quiet, I guess.

You mentioned you don't get restless or fidgety, but I want to make sure I'm not missing anything. As a child, did you ever have trouble waiting your turn, or would you interrupt others or jump into activities without being asked?
Um, no... I don't think I did that. I didn't really have trouble waiting or anything. Like I said, I was pretty quiet, so... I didn't really interrupt people.

When you're trying to organize your work or keep track of multiple things you need to do, do you find it hard to get started or to arrange things in order? Like, do you struggle with planning out steps, or do things just feel disorganized in your head?

Um... yeah, I guess so. Things get pretty messy. Like... my apartment and my laptop, they're just... full of half-started things. Rent papers, notes from the gallery, PDFs for articles, to-do lists just... everywhere. It's hard to know where to start. I just... I can't really figure out what needs to happen first. So it just stays like that.

When you were younger, did you ever feel like your mind was racing or jumping from one thought to another really quickly, even if you were sitting still? Or did you find it hard to stop yourself from doing things once you got an idea?
Um... no. Not really. I don't remember my mind racing like that. I didn't really have ideas I had to act on right away. I was mostly just... spaced out, I guess. Not really jumping around.
When you're trying to focus on something, do you find yourself getting lost in your own thoughts or daydreaming, even when there's nothing going on around you to distract you?

Um... yeah, I guess. When I'm trying to read or write at my desk... I'll just get caught up in a random thought. Like about an exhibit idea or something. And then... I don't know, twenty minutes go by before I even notice I stopped working. 

It doesn't even have to be a thought, really... it could just be a siren outside, or... people talking in the hallway. It all just... pulls me away.
When you think back to elementary school and middle school, would you say you were having these same attention and organization problems back then, or did they start later on?

Um... yeah. I guess it was kind of the same back then. My teachers... they would always write on my report cards that I had good ideas, but... I'd forget to turn in worksheets. Or I'd lose the instructions for things. I missed a lot of little details, I guess. My parents pretty much had to check my backpack every night to make sure I actually did things. So... yeah, it's been a while.
